intro: Mauritius is an Indian Ocean island that had no people until Europeans arrived, and is famous as the home of the dodo.

chapters.title: The dodo
text: Arab and Portuguese sailors knew of the island, but the Dutch settled first in 1638. The flightless dodo, found only here, was extinct by about 1681, a symbol of human-caused extinction.

highlight.title: Extinct
highlight.text: 'Dead as a dodo' became a saying for something gone for ever.

chapters.title: French and British rule
text: France took over in 1715 and brought enslaved people from Africa and Madagascar to work sugar plantations. Britain captured the island in 1810. After slavery ended in 1835, about half a million indentured labourers came from India.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Mauritius became independent in 1968 and a republic in 1992. It is one of Africa's most stable democracies. In 2025 Britain agreed to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.

timeline.title: Chagos deal
timeline.text: Britain agrees to transfer the islands.

keyTerms.meaning: Workers bound by contract for years.
